# Get Started

Download Emaki, install an agent, and open a project.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The four buttons bring their panels beside the chat.

1.  ### Download Emaki

    [**macOS** Apple silicon](https://github.com/alkaline-software/emaki/releases/latest/download/Emaki-mac-arm64.dmg) [**macOS** Intel](https://github.com/alkaline-software/emaki/releases/latest/download/Emaki-mac-x64.dmg) [**Windows** x64 installer](https://github.com/alkaline-software/emaki/releases/latest/download/Emaki-windows-x64-setup.exe) [**Linux** x64 AppImage](https://github.com/alkaline-software/emaki/releases/latest/download/Emaki-linux-x64.AppImage)

    The Mac image is signed and notarized and needs macOS 14 or later. Windows is unsigned, so SmartScreen asks once: *More info*, then *Run anyway*. On Linux run the AppImage, or install the `.deb` from the [release page](https://github.com/alkaline-software/emaki/releases/latest). From then on the app updates itself.

2.  ### Install an agent

    Emaki works with Claude Code and Codex. Install one or both, and sign in.

    **Claude Code**

    [Install it](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code), then run `claude` once to sign in.

    **Codex**

    [Install it](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli), then run `codex` once to sign in.

    Not sure what this machine has? The Agents page (⌘E) checks, and walks you through installing one, a step at a time, with a shell beside the steps.

3.  ### GitHub, if you want it

    Git is optional. With it, Emaki shows a project’s changes and branches and commits for you; signed in to GitHub, it fetches, pulls and pushes too. The Agents page has the steps: install git, sign in with `gh`, and tell git who your commits are by.

## Open a project

Pick a folder, choose the agent, and type. That is a session, in that folder, and its tab and its row in the sidebar appear at once. Or pick up one the agent already has: every session on the machine is listed under its project, from both agents. The first launch copies every Claude Code transcript into `~/.emaki/archive`, and each later launch catches up, so a session the agent has deleted is still here. See [Projects](../docs/projects.llms.md).

## The window

The chat is the main panel. Four panels stand beside it, a button and a key each, there when you want them and gone when you do not.

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
| [Files](../docs/files.llms.md) | ⌘⇧F | the project’s folder as a tree, a pane for any file, and git |
| [Outline](../docs/outline.llms.md) | ⌘⇧O | a label for every prompt, to jump back to any step |
| [Shell Terminal](../docs/shell.llms.md) | ⌘⇧S | a shell in the project’s folder |
| [Agent Terminal](../docs/agent.llms.md) | ⌘⇧A | the session’s own agent as it runs |

Files and outline share the left side, one at a time; the two terminals share the right.

## What it keeps

Everything is under `~/.emaki`:

|               |                                                 |
|---------------|-------------------------------------------------|
| `archive/`    | every Claude Code session, copied byte for byte |
| `logs/`       | each session rendered as markdown               |
| `search.db`   | the full-text index                             |
| `config.json` | your settings                                   |

Only `archive/` cannot be rebuilt. That is the folder to back up.

Emaki sets one thing in Claude Code’s settings: its status line, which feeds the [status bar](../docs/chats.llms.md#the-status-bar) under the composer. `emaki-core statusline restore` puts yours back.
